problem: Let $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where ${b}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=2{c}_{1}?$
worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={c}_{1}+3{c}_{2} \\  & =3{c}_{2}+{c}_{1} \\  & =3\cdot 3(\frac{1}{3}{c}_{2})+\frac{1}{2}(2{c}_{1}) \\  & =9{b}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].$
